In this appeal, we are not to see if that judgment is correct, but we are to see whether the adverse finding in that judgment of the two previous suit operates as res judicata in the instant suit. Mr. Pal has contended that it will not operate as res judicate in that those two suits were dismissed so far as defendant Chandra Bala was concerned and that as there was no occasion for her'  to challenge those findings in appeal this finding cannot be accepted as final to operate 1S res judicata. In support of this contention he has relied upon a number of cases. The first case he has referred to is Midnapore Zamindary Co. v. Naresh Chandra Roy, AIR 1922 PC 241. In that case a landlord sued his tenant for khas possession but the tenant took the aplca of occupancy right. In a previous suit by the landlord's father against the tenant the same pica of his occupancy right was taken along with a plea that the suit was not maintainable being 'premature'. The plea of occupancy right was rejected, but the other plea that the, suit was premature and therefore not maintainable was accepted and the suit was dismissed. In the subsequent suit the question arose whether the decision in the earlier suit that the tenant had no occupancy right would be a res judicata.
